newsitem.title: ESTONIA: TALLINNA Q1 PROFIT 18.8 MLN KROONS.
newsitem.headline: TALLINNA Q1 PROFIT 18.8 MLN KROONS.

text.p: Estonia's Tallinna Pank said on Thursday that its first quarter net profit was 18.8 million kroons.
The bank said in a statement that the profit in March was 149,000 kroons.
The bank said the March profit was low as it wrote off the loss of sale of its TH Ferries loan to Talinvest.
"The profit might have been even bigger but speculation in the media had a bad affect on the bank's financial activity," Tallinna Pank chairman of the board, Rait Luukas, said in the statement.
Newspaper Aripaev in March reported that the bank was facing a crisis of confidence in the local market due to worries over the loan although Tallinna Pank denied there were any problems.
Tallinna Pank's first quarter results were 5.8 million kroons better thank excpeted, Lukas said.
Tallinna Pank earned most of its profits from stock market trading in January but traditional profit sources had a bigger role during the following two months, he added.
The bank made a loss of 10 million kroons on the TH loan.
Tallinna Pank's total assets decreased by 1.1 percent or 24.7 million kroons during the first quarter. In March, assets grew by 1.4 percent or 30.5 million kroons.
The bank's total equity grew by 18.8 million kroons after the first quarter profit.
Liabilities fell by 43.5 million kroons, including a fall of 24.7 million kroons in amounts owed to credit institutions.
Demand deposits showed an increase of 4.2 percent or 15.6 million kroons while time deposits decreased 38.7 million kroons in the first quarter.
Tallinna Pank decreased short-term loans from Estonian money market by 113.4 million kroons. At the same time, credits from foreign institutions rose by 89.6 million kroons.
"As they are mostly long-term funds, they will, in addition to spreading risk, give additional security to the bank's financing base," the bank said.
On the asset side, the loan portfolio decreased by 61.3 million kroons, which was in accordance with bank's board decision on the principles of forming assets, the bank said.
Loan provisions made up 1.3 percent of loan portfolio. Loan portfolio constituted 55.1 percent of assets.
Tallinna Pank average loan interest rate continued falling - compared to 14.4 percent at the end of last year, it had fallen to 13.7 percent at the end of first quarter.
Tallinna Pank last year consolidated net profit was 50.4 million kroons or 52 percent up from 1995.
Tallinna Pank excpects its profit to be 87.3 million kroons for this year.
-- Eva Palu, Tallinn newsroom, +372 630 8400, reuters@reuters.ee
